newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 27.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- The Dow Jones Industrials rose 23.83 to 6546.68, their second-highest close ever.
- A settlement of the General Motors C/K pickup class action suit was approved by a Louisiana judge.
- General Mills won antitrust clearance for its $570 million purchase of Chex from Ralcorp.
- Digital TV standards were cleared by the FCC.
- Caterpillar is facing hundreds of NLRB complaints of alleged labor law violations.
- The SEC approved a rule designed to protect the public from abusive telemarketing by muni-bond peddlers.
- A group of TV broadcasters sued satellite programming firm PrimeTime 24, accusing the Great Universal unit of illegally providing network shows to some satellite dish owners.
- Federal courts are trimming punitive damage awards in the months since the Supreme Court ruled that a man was not entitled to $2 million because his BMW had a bad paint job.
- Montgomery Ward named Toys R Us executive Roger Goddu as chairman and CEO.
- Short interest rose 4.1 percent to another record in the latest month for stocks on the Nasdaq Stock Market.
- Westinghouse Electric received FCC approval for its $3.9 billion purchase of Infinity Broadcasting.
- Computer Associates said revenue for the quarter ending Tuesday will fall short of analysts expectations.
- PSINet said it will have a positive cash flow for the first time early next year.
- The bond market barely got off the dime on the day after Christmas, with the price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closing unchanged from Tuesday in thin trading.
- In what could foreshadow a turn-around for the recently pounded steel sector, insiders at four U.S. steel producers have been purchasing shares.
